Subject: Spike in 502s and p99 at EOD batch — urgent

Hi Jasmine,

We just saw our nightly EOD batch (22:45 PDT) cause a large spike in p99 latency across our on‑prem Redwood deployment and ~12% 502 error rate for token generation for ~18 minutes. This is the first time it's hit this level in weeks. It blocked downstream reporting jobs and triggered pager duty.

Attached are a trimmed set of logs and the sequence IDs where we saw the failures. We need a root cause and mitigation plan now — customers are impacted and our ops team is asking for exec visibility. Can you please escalate?

Immediate asks:
- Short-term mitigation: can you route traffic to hosted fallback or a dedicated pool?
- Quick RCA: any known regressions to runtime or kernel selection?
- Exec sync: Noah (CTO) and our head of ops want a 9:30am PDT sync tomorrow.

Thanks,

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 00:38:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 502s and p99 at EOD batch — urgent

Quick triage notes (from initial log sweep):
- Observed repeated KV cache evictions on the primary inference nodes for tenant solstice-labs during the 22:40–23:00 window. Evictions correlate with sudden memory pressure spikes on GPU host (OOM killer not triggered, but mem_cgroup churn high).
- Token generation latencies show increased kernel scheduling waits (sched_latency) and a pattern of repeated fallback to FP32 kernels for a subset of models. This suggests a quantization selection mismatch at high concurrency.
- 502s are originating from our inference proxy hitting a 30s downstream request timeout when the GPU queue length surges.

Immediate mitigations I propose (can be executed in this order):
A) Apply a temporary routing policy: divert new EOD batch traffic to dedicated burst pool (if enabled), or to hosted fallback for non-PII batches; throttle concurrency to reduce queue depth.
B) Increase KV cache allocations for solstice-labs (config tweak) to avoid cache thrash during short bursts.
C) Force kernel selection to the previously stable quantized path for the model version they pinned (model-v3-q4).

I will attach a small flamegraph and a trimmed trace for the busiest window. If we do A and B quickly we should see p99 drop within one batch iteration.

— Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
(Attachments: p99_trace_flamegraph.svg)

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, Emma Carter <emma@solstice.io>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 01:05:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in 502s and p99 at EOD batch — urgent

Emma / team — I kicked off two actions:
- Routing change: temporarily routing non‑PII batch traffic to our hosted fallback for the next two batch windows. This preserves throughput for critical downstream reporting.
- KV cache increase: bumped solstice-labs cache allocation by +25% on the assigned host pool; propagation should be immediate.

Early observations: after the routing/flushing actions, we saw a reduction in queue depth and a drop in 502s in the subsequent 10 minutes of soft traffic. Will monitor the next EOD run closely.

Planning for the 9:30am sync: I’ll bring histograms for token latencies, kernel selection breakdown, and a proposed permanent config change if the quantized path needs to be forced.

— Priyom Das
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
